title: He Was Clinically Blind on One Side, Yet Pointed to Lights 90% Right

acts.name: London 1974: Pitch-Dark Left Field Yet Uncanny Pointing
sentences: Clinically blind on his left side, Patient D.B. swore half the room was pitch dark!
Then his doctor flashed a silent dot into that dark half.
Patient D.B. insisted he saw nothing at all.
Asked to point anyway — his finger landed dead-on!
In nineteen seventy-four, London doctors witnessed that exact shock.
Brain surgery in London saved young Patient D.B.'s life.
Yet it removed his right primary visual cortex, the vision center.
Everything left of his nose vanished into blankness.
Here is what went wrong with textbook rules of sight.

acts.name: Weiskrantz's 'Just Guess' Test & 90% Blind Accuracy
sentences: Lawrence Weiskrantz and Elizabeth Warrington tested him in London.
Both eyes and pupils stayed completely healthy.
Flashing light into his blind left side drew silence.
He reported nothing at all on every trial.
Then Weiskrantz asked him simply to reach and guess.
His hand pointed to unseen targets ninety percent right, like nine of ten coins!
Shown giant X or O shapes, he guessed ninety percent again, like an ace!
Laughing in disbelief, he thought he failed every try!
Blind inside yet pointing true — for him, this was a total nightmare.

acts.name: Ancient Reflex Detour: 10% Eye Fibers Bypass Main Screen
sentences: How could blind darkness guide an accurate human hand?
Ninety percent of eye wires, like nine of ten lanes, hit back cortex.
When surgery removed that wall, conscious pictures vanished.
Yet ten percent of the optic nerve — the eye cable — branches off early!
Those older fibers dive straight into the brainstem — your reflex center.
Another shortcut hops across the thalamus — your sensory relay station.
Ancient fish and frogs steered whole lives with that path!
Your reflex map tracks motion without waking awareness.
Could someone completely blind walk through a crowded hall?

acts.name: Single-Screen Camera Myth vs Emotional Blindsight
sentences: People assume human vision works like one television screen.
Smash the main screen, and every visual skill should die.
Skeptics claimed stray room light explained those London guesses.
Careful controls with dimmed rooms crushed the stray-light excuse.
In two thousand eight, Beatrice de Gelder tested total blindness.
Two strokes had wiped out both back hemispheres completely.
Without a cane, Patient T.N. saw zero shapes or edges.
What happened when researchers filled a long hallway with obstacles?

acts.name: 2008 Obstacle Hallway Walk Without One Bump Climax
sentences: Researchers scattered chairs, boxes, and tripods down a corridor.
They asked the blind walker simply to stroll straight ahead.
Without one cane tap, he weaved past every chair!
His shoulders angled sideways through narrow box gaps cleanly.
He crossed the entire obstacle course with zero collisions!
Shown faces on screen, his emotional alarm even matched smiles!
The researchers were left completely stunned.
Instead of one screen, two parallel vision streams run inside you.

acts.name: Flinching Before Seeing & Trusting Quiet Reflexes
sentences: Have you felt your hidden reflex sight?
Ever duck a fast ball before naming it?
Your reflex shortcut flinches milliseconds faster than a blink!
Conscious pictures arrive moments after your hand moves.
In stroke clinics, guessing drills train spared pathways.
Sight is richer than the picture you narrate.
Beneath awareness, ancient guardian circuits watch every step.
Which proves your eyes know more than your mind admits.
